answers.note: Strong, accurate indicative content and a genuinely analytical Level 5 model extract, but the extract-based question does not actually print an extract and there is little guidance on placing an answer within a level.

Sound levels and indicative content, but the 'extract' is a single line with an apparently spliced-in phrase ('I am so fluttered and so glad!') and there is no guidance at all on placing answers within a level.

A complete, AQA-faithful pack with a correctly quoted extract, AO-mapped six-level descriptors, explicit within-level placement and capping rules, and an annotated model that analyses methods with accurate embedded quotations and integrated context.

Concise and student-facing, it praises the specific figures, names the single priority (explain why each term angered Germans), prompts rather than rewrites, and ends with a short focused rewrite task.

Encouraging and accurate on the main weakness, but it gives five numbered improvements, writes model sentences and a conclusion for the student, and sets a full rewrite rather than a short task (it also credits the student with naming the war guilt clause, which they did not).

Tight, well-judged feedback with specific strengths, one clearly labelled priority, guiding questions plus a sentence starter rather than a rewrite, a useful accuracy note on the 1921 figure, and a timed 10-minute task.

Correct percentages and share-of-loss figures with sensible ranking by fixability, but diagnosis is limited to a blanks-versus-wrong-answers check and the stated lesson allocations (5/3/1/1) do not match the 10-lesson sequence given.

The strongest analysis: accurate percentages and totals (359/616, 254/359, about 3 marks per student), a ranking explicitly weighing loss against teachability, a likely-cause column plus script checks for blanks, partial method marks and student profiles, and a 10-lesson plan with retrieval starters.

Arithmetic and per-question likely causes are correct, but it ranks by size of loss only, spreads the 10 lessons across all eight topics instead of choosing a few, and has little retrieval to keep stronger topics ticking over.
